detailed_rationale:
KPR Mill is one of India's largest vertically integrated apparel manufacturers - spinning yarn through to knitted fabric and finished garments - with a diversified income cushion from sugar/molasses/ethanol and wind power, plus smaller automotive-adjacent subsidiaries. The quality_score of 91.3 (near the top of the entire universe) is earned: ROE around 15.7-19.9% depending on period, ROCE ~19.6-24.1%, debt cut sharply (borrowings down to Rs 596cr from Rs 1,348cr in FY25), and interest coverage over 24x. FY26 delivered Rs 6,650cr sales and Rs 866cr net profit, with Q4 FY26 alone at Rs 1,785cr sales / Rs 227cr PAT / 20% OPM - a genuinely well-run, financially disciplined operator.

The growth side of the picture is much softer: revenue_cagr_3y of only 2.4% and revenue_growth_1y of 4.1% (both among the weakest growth scores in the universe, 17.2 and 21.4 respectively) show a business that has essentially plateaued in scale even as its balance sheet and margins stay excellent. Sector context explains part of this: Indian cotton yarn and garment exporters have been navigating a volatile couple of years - US tariff-policy uncertainty (announced tariffs under the Trump administration hit KPR and export peers like Gokaldas Exports and Kitex Garments hard when announced), offset partially by a government customs duty exemption on cotton imports that boosted textile stocks broadly, and yarn prices have since started rising again on demand pressure. Current industry-level expectations for cotton yarn makers point to high-single-digit revenue growth (9-11%) with 150-250bps of margin expansion as pricing realizations improve - a reasonable proxy for what a scaled, well-run name like KPR should be able to at least match.

Ownership shows a long, gradual promoter dilution (74.90% in Mar 2017 down to 67.52% now, a ~7.4 point reduction over three years alone per the latest window) - a trend to note but not itself alarming for a company that just approved a 250% dividend payout, showing continued willingness to return cash. FII holding has been rising (to 7.02%) alongside steady DII ownership (~19.25%).
recommendation_rationale: Quant recommendation is Hold on both windows, and the fundamentals support staying there: this is genuinely one of the higher-quality operators in the scorecard universe (quality_score 91.3), but growth has stalled to low-single-digits and the stock trades at ~43-44x earnings - a valuation that assumes a growth re-acceleration the recent numbers have not yet delivered. Excellent quality alone doesn't justify a stronger call when paired with this growth profile and multiple; equally, the balance sheet strength and sector-improving pricing backdrop rule out anything as negative as a Sell.
summary: KPR Mill is a well-run, vertically integrated Indian yarn-to-garment manufacturer with a strong balance sheet (debt more than halved in the last year) and diversified income from sugar and ethanol. Revenue growth has slowed to low-single-digits recently, partly reflecting a tough couple of years for Indian textile exporters (US tariff uncertainty, volatile cotton/yarn pricing), even as industry conditions now look to be improving. At over 40x earnings for a business growing only mid-single-digits, we rate it a Hold - excellent quality, but not cheap for the growth on offer today.
positive_para: KPR Mill's balance sheet and capital discipline are genuinely best-in-class for the sector - debt cut by more than half in a year, ROCE comfortably above 19%, and a 250% dividend just approved - while the broader cotton yarn industry backdrop is turning more constructive (customs duty relief on cotton imports, rising yarn prices, industry-wide margin expansion expected). A scaled, vertically integrated operator like KPR is typically the name best positioned to capture that recovery disproportionately.
negative_para: The plain fact is growth has stalled - 3-year revenue CAGR of just 2.4% and 1-year growth of 4.1% are among the weakest growth readings in the entire scorecard universe, for a stock still priced at ~43-44x earnings. Export-oriented names like KPR remain exposed to US trade-policy risk (tariff announcements have already hit the stock and its peers meaningfully once), and until the sector's improving pricing/demand backdrop actually shows up as revenue acceleration rather than industry commentary, the current multiple is being paid mostly on the strength of the balance sheet and past execution, not on demonstrated current growth.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~43-44x earnings against 2-4% recent revenue growth, the market is implicitly pricing a return to KPR's historically stronger growth rates - which the improving sector backdrop (cotton duty relief, firming yarn prices, industry-wide 9-11% revenue growth expectations) makes plausible but not yet proven in KPR's own numbers. This reads as a quality premium being paid ahead of the growth actually showing up; fair only if the sector recovery materializes as forecast, rich if the export/tariff overhang persists.
